outgoing.name: Algebra
outgoing.excerpt: She received a rather desultory education, and mastered algebra and Euclid in secret after she had left school, and without any external help.

outgoing.name: Astronomy
outgoing.excerpt: She studied mathematics and astronomy, and became the second woman scientist to receive recognition in the United Kingdom after Caroline Herschel.

outgoing.name: Italy
outgoing.excerpt: In 1838 she and her husband went to Italy, where she spent much of the rest of her life.

outgoing.name: Mathematics
outgoing.excerpt: She studied mathematics and astronomy, and became the second woman scientist to receive recognition in the United Kingdom after Caroline Herschel.

outgoing.name: Russia
outgoing.excerpt: In 1804 she married her distant cousin, the Russian Consul in London, Captain Samuel Greig, who died in 1806; they had two children.
